messages.subject: Re: sequenza.extract error
messages.body_plain:
Hi Francesco,

I have tested one file using both parallel or single mode and the results are consistent between each other, however the results are not the same as I expected (third party test). I am wondering does it have anything to do with the input BAM: I am using duplicate-removed, re-calibrated BAM files, does it matter? Thanks.

Huilei

On Thu, Aug 31, 2017 at 9:42 AM, Francesco Favero <favero.f...@gmail.com> wrote:
> I do not guarantee it will not effected the estimation at all, it actually give a slightly different CP image, but the preferred solution is the same - in the test I’ve run -
>
> Francesco
>
> > On 31 Aug 2017, at 15.30, huilei xu <huil...@gmail.com> wrote:
> >
> > Thank you, I will tweak your code and give it a try, good to know the estimation result won't be affected whether taking the whole data or breaking down by chromosome.
> >
> > On Thu, Aug 31, 2017 at 9:23 AM, Francesco Favero <favero.f...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > Hi,
> > >
> > > I’ve seen you also opened an issue about the parallel processing.
> > > I think it’s possible, however it may be too convoluted to include the support in the package.
> > >
> > > Basically, you could easily run sequenza.extract for a single chromosome in parallel, then run for each object sequenza.fit, separately.
> > > Each sequenza.fit instance will give a separate CP object
> > > The CP object, is a list with the info:
> > >     ploidy: A numeric vector of tested ploidy values
> > >     cellularity: A numeric vector of tested cellularity values
> > >     lpp: Anumeric matrix of log-posterior probability for each (ploidy, cellularity) pair.
> > >
> > > Be aware that sequenza.fit may fail if there are no segments to feed the model, so you may setup some error checking try() to fallback to a default CP object, with all 0s in the lpp matrix (or some other approach you may end up with).
> > >
> > >
> > > The lpp of all the resulting CP objects can be sum to get the “final” CP object, which would equivalent to the CP object as you had run the program sequentially.
> > >
> > > It may be a little overhead, but it should work :). I’m not expert on how to parallelize this, I would do something like:
> > >
> > > > library(sequenza)
> > > > library(parallel)
> > > >
> > > > data.file <- system.file("data", "example.seqz.txt.gz",
> > > >     package = "sequenza")
> > > >
> > > > chromosome <- c(1:22, c("X", "Y"))
> > > >
> > > > n_cpu = 4 # or any other amount of parallel processes you want
> > > >
> > > > sample_stats <- gc.sample.stats(data.file)
> > > >
> > > > extract_chroms <- mclapply(chromosome, FUN = function(x, seqz_file, gc_stats) {
> > > >         sequenza.extract(seqz_file, chromosome.list = x, gc.stats= gc_stats)
> > > >     },
> > > >     seqz_file = data.file, gc_stats = sample_stats, mc.cores = n_cpu)
> > > >
> > > >
> > > > CP_chroms <- mclapply(extract_chroms, FUN = function(x) {
> > > >  sequenza.fit(x, mc.cores = 1) # adjust mc.cores, beware that each process
> > > >                                # will try to use the number of cpu you set
> > > >                                # here so it will fork exponentially
> > > > }, mc.cores = n_cpu)
> > > >
> > > > CP_chroms_lpp <- sapply(1:length(CP_chroms), FUN = function(x, y) y[[x]]["lpp"], y = CP_chroms)
> > > > CP_chroms_lpp[is.na <http://is.na/>(CP_chroms_lpp)] <- NULL
> > > > CP_lpp <- Reduce("+", CP_chroms_lpp)
> > > >
> > > > CP <- list(cellularity = CP_chroms[[1]]$cellularity, ploidy = CP_chroms[[1]]$ploidy, lpp = CP_lpp)
> > > > cp.plot(CP)
> > > > cp.plot.contours(CP, add = T)
> > > >
> > > > res <- get.ci <http://get.ci/>(CP)
> > > >
> > > > res$max.cellularity
> > > >
> > > > res$max.ploidy
> > > >
> > >
> > > Francesco
> > >
> > >
> > >
> > > > On 30 Aug 2017, at 19.53, huilei xu <huil...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > >
> > > > Hi Francesco,
> > > >
> > > > The updated cleanup version works so far (It is now processing chr #9). One irrelevant question: is there a way in the sequenza R package to parallel processing different chromosome and combine the results somehow to boost the speed? My goal is purity estimation only (no need to get CNV). Thank you.
> > > >
> > > > On Wed, Aug 30, 2017 at 9:52 AM, Francesco Favero <favero.f...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > > > Hi,
> > > > >
> > > > > I’ve actually just pushed a commit to fix it in the cleanup branch.
> > > > > https://bitbucket.org/sequenza_tools/sequenza/commits/2d6c85e5a227a1524c153f25e458dde6752a1173
> > > > >
> > > > > Can you try to install the cleanup branch and see if the bug is resolved?
> > > > >
> > > > > library(devtools)
> > > > > install_bitbucket("sequenza_tools/sequenza@cleanup")
> > > > >
> > > > >
> > > > > Thanks
> > > > >
> > > > > Francesco
> > > > >
> > > > >
> > > > > > On 30 Aug 2017, at 15.47, huilei xu <huil...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > > > >
> > > > > > Hi,
> > > > > >
> > > > > > I have tested both on 2.1.2 and 2.1.0 version, which gave me the same error msg:
> > > > > >
> > > > > > test <- sequenza.extract('my.seqz.gz')
> > > > > > Processing 1: Error in data.frame(base.count = as.integer(n.base.mut), maj.base.freq = as.numeric(max.freqs[, : arguments imply differing number of rows: 1962, 235

> > > > > > I think the error comes from mut.fractions step that generates unequal length of n.base.mut vs max.freqs due to isgnoring . NA rows. My original bam files are sorted.recalibrated bam and it's using human genome hs37d5. Thank you.

messages.subject: Re: suggest about selecting normal loci based on normal cnv
messages.subject_clean: suggest about selecting normal loci based on normal cnv
messages.body_plain:
Hi Francesco,

Sorry for late reply.

When I wrote INDEL, I actually wanted to say copy gain of loss region. It's a wrongly used word, but I think you got my point according to your reply.

I find the reason that the ploidy was overestimated on my data. Actually, I am studying transmissable tumor. If the host is with high heterozygosity, the segment method "het" is over sensitive, resuliting to lots of segments, also the cnv status between host and tumor is genetically unrelated. Totally, these reasons lead to a summing noisy effect when estimating plodiy. I am try using "fast" segment method and large pcf value, and it seems better to reflect reality.

BTW
sequenza CRAN version is still 2.1.2, but bitbucket version is higher. I tried your devel version to see if any improvement was pushed, but I found no ducument for sequenza.extract/fit/results. It's hard for me to read the souce code, waiting for your stable update.

Thank you for on-going coding! Best wishes!

On Monday, May 29, 2017 at 7:33:43 PM UTC+8, Francesco Favero wrote:

> Dear Xuan,
>
> Thanks for your input. |I actually think assessing the normal-only cnv state is a lacking point in the current pipeline.
> I’m working on a new version that treats normal and tumor separately (we solved a memory issue that was preventing it before).
> That at least would give the possibility of visual inspection if the CNV are present in the normal.
>
> The preprocessing step,in its current state, is ditching completely the indels calls (either somatic or germlines), We could in principle test if they can be taken into account to discard or give less a given region…
> We could make additional check in the pipeline to deselective/penalise genomic regions with germline indels/cna
> In practice is not so easy to systematically model - principally due to the variance expected from sample to sample (not patients, just sequencing data in general), and the various bias may have different causes.
>
> Thanks again for your valuable input, I hope to have more update on the topic soon
>
> Best
>
> Francesco
>

> > On 16 May 2017, at 16.05, Xuan Wang <xmasw...@gmail.com> wrote:
> >

> > Dear Francesco,
> >
> > I used sequenza on my species' data, which genome has massive complex SVs. The recommended ploidy of some samples range from 4 to 6, but it should be 2 according to the karyotype FISH analysis. And the CNV profile also become doubled following the tetraploid or hexaploid estimation. I also tried by adjusting some parameters, but there wasn't any big changes.
> > I think your grid-based max bayes inferring model is absolutely reasonable, except the assumption of the constat normal ploidy. From paper nature19823, I get enlighten that they call CNV on normal sample, then exclude the loci in INDEL region in normal sample before estimating ploidy and cellularity. From my knowledge, sequenza will be unbiased if the normal ploidy changes are considered.
> > Expect your opinion and updates :)
> >
> > Best!
> > Xuan
> >

messages.subject: Sequenza CNV calling only for human and not for other species?!! e.g. mouse mm10
messages.subject_clean: Sequenza CNV calling only for human and not for other species?!! e.g. mouse mm10
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I have used Sequenza for mouse whole exome sequencing data (mm10). I followed the instructions form the vignette and was using the VarScan2 snp and cnv output to create a seqz object. Everything worked fine.
However, just by chance, I noticed that the function 'sequenza.extract' implicitly assumes the assembly is hg19! There is no warning about this in the vignette. When trying it with specifically setting assembly=mm10, I get an error:

# Now extract the info from the seqz data test

> sequenza.extract(seqz_data_out_seqz, gz = F, assembly = "mm10")
Processing 1: Error : assembly must be one of hg19, hg18, hg17 or hg16 Error in if (!is.null(breaks) & nrow(breaks) > 0) { :

  argument is of length zero

Calls: sequenza.extract
Execution halted

Could you let me know whether the assembly really matters for the extract function? I'm assuming it is not usable for mouse, and if that's true, there should be a warning about this in the vignette and/or in the extract function. But maybe I am misinterpreting something?

Thanks for your answer!

Best wishes,
Ariane
